# Even stronger teachers can teach the wrong thing: evidence, compatibility, and preserving success

[简体中文](../../../../learning/deep-dives/post-training/teacher-and-context.md) · English

Updated 2026-11-12 · 52 topic entries / 11 representative comparisons

Teacher value is more than aggregate score. OPSD changes training visibility, MOPD and token routing organize multiple teachers, CSD aligns probability events, SPOD protects successful student actions, and VAD isolates corrections attributable to visual evidence. Verify these constraints independently before imitation.

[Mechanisms](#comparison) · [Trade-offs](#analysis) · [Cross-paper questions](#questions) · [Updates](#updates)

!!! note "How to read this card"

    The table compares representative methods. It is not a shared-benchmark leaderboard. Teaching examples are not measured results.

Axes: Teacher source: a privileged same-weight view or independent domain experts · Combination granularity: domains, token routing, and successful action protection · Comparable interfaces: shared vocabulary coordinates or common text events · Attribution: privileged evidence, language priors, and existing student skills

## Trade-off analysis {#analysis}

### Check whether teacher signals describe the same event before mixing

MOPD and token routing can mix teachers but differ in domain-level and per-position selection. With different tokenizers, CSD first aligns decoded text events rather than mixing coordinates directly. OPSD can use the same model with extra conditions instead of adding independent experts.

Sources: [MOPD](../../../../post-training/2606.30406-mopd/README-en.md) · [Compatibility Matters: A Framework for Token-Level Teacher Selection in On-Policy Distillation](../../../../post-training/2610.21234-token-teacher-selection/README-en.md) · [CSD: Common-Support Distillation for Cross-Tokenizer Knowledge Transfer](../../../../post-training/2610.28895-csd/README-en.md) · [OPSD](../../../../post-training/2601.18734-opsd/README-en.md)

### Teacher corrections should be examined rather than accepted wholesale

SPOD protects specific successful actions the teacher disfavors, not whole successful episodes. VAD asks whether a privileged correction comes from visual evidence or shared language bias. Student success and evidence attribution are separate checks even when the teacher scores higher overall.

Sources: [Beyond the Teacher: Understanding and Preserving Distillation Overshoot in Agentic On-Policy Distillation](../../../../post-training/2610.25034-spod/README-en.md) · [VAD](../../../../post-training/2607.28590-vad/README-en.md) · [OPSD](../../../../post-training/2601.18734-opsd/README-en.md)

### Teachers can supply logits and parameter directions, but the evidence paths are distinct

MOPD organizes domain-teacher supervision on student trajectories; P²-MOPD additionally retains task vectors from the expert bank as continuously learned directions. Teacher selection determines who supplies token feedback, whereas parameter priors also change movement in weight space. Free B can leave the task-vector span while coefficients learn low-dimensional directions, and export remains a single student. The paper's support-restricted MOPD surrogate, shared unclipped gradient and two-channel optimizer ordering have separate contracts; a legacy candidate-mixture interface is not that complete training pipeline.

Sources: [P²-MOPD: Accelerating Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation via Parameter Priors](../../../../post-training/2611.03953-p2-mopd/README-en.md) · [MOPD](../../../../post-training/2606.30406-mopd/README-en.md)

### Where privileged context acts matters as much as whether a teacher exists

OPSD separates student-visible problems from teacher-only references. Targeted Guidance instead inserts feedback before failed turns and restricts auxiliary reverse KL to those turns while retaining ordinary criterion RL. Sparse gating chooses gradient locations; whole-response-token normalization controls each rollout's overall scale. They are not equivalent to dropping tokens and recomputing a mean. Exact recovery of the original RL loss without failures is a numerical contract, not evidence that feedback was screened or coding improved.

Sources: [Stabilizing On-Policy Targeted Guidance in Agentic Reinforcement Learning](../../../../post-training/2611.05266-targeted-guidance/README-en.md) · [OPSD](../../../../post-training/2601.18734-opsd/README-en.md)

### Does extra information condition the teacher or merely define a training label?

OPSD gives a verified solution to a same-weights teacher that predicts a vocabulary distribution at the student's prefix. Targeted Guidance inserts judgment feedback only before failed turns, alongside the usual RL reward. RAGCompass uses reference answers only to label candidate evidence sets by offline reader F1; its supervision is over whole candidates, not tokens. None permits training-only information to leak into inference.

Sources: [RAGCompass: Generalizable Retriever Routing via Reranking](../../../../post-training/2611.05596-ragcompass/README-en.md) · [OPSD](../../../../post-training/2601.18734-opsd/README-en.md) · [Stabilizing On-Policy Targeted Guidance in Agentic Reinforcement Learning](../../../../post-training/2611.05266-targeted-guidance/README-en.md)

### Constructing a reference-free teacher differs from permanently relying on a privileged view

OPSD gives the teacher a verified solution while the student sees its own prefixes. BOPD first internalizes that supervision in intermediate parameters, then uses the reference-free intermediate to teach a student restored from its initial checkpoint. It is not continued Stage I student training, and privileged Stage I scores cannot become reference-free Stage II supervision by caching. Frozen weights can still predict differently on new student prefixes; stage, context and parameter provenance remain separate.

Sources: [Bootstrapped On-Policy Distillation](../../../../post-training/2611.13680-bopd/README-en.md) · [OPSD](../../../../post-training/2601.18734-opsd/README-en.md)

### Protecting successful episodes and particular actions within them creates different update sets

The LCS method excludes every successful student episode and chooses same-task corrective references for failures. SPOD can still train successful episodes, suppressing KL and adding a soft floor only where the teacher's complete-action probability is below the student's. The former also changes reference information; the latter changes action-level supervision. A generic success mask cannot replace their distinct denominators, probability conditions and gates. Training success references remain hidden from evaluated students.

Sources: [Which Successes Make Good References? Action-Sequence Alignment for Multi-Turn On-Policy Distillation](../../../../post-training/2611.13135-lcs-reference-opd/README-en.md) · [Beyond the Teacher: Understanding and Preserving Distillation Overshoot in Agentic On-Policy Distillation](../../../../post-training/2610.25034-spod/README-en.md)

## Cross-paper questions {#questions}

Try answering before expanding the explanation. Each question relates at least two papers.

### Why isn't same-weight OPSD just letting the student copy verified answers? {#cross-same-weights-privileged-view}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Conditions differ. The student only reads the question and generates its own prefix; the training teacher reads a verified answer before scoring that prefix. Supervision targets an unprivileged student. MOPD instead uses independent domain teachers. Neither can feed training answers into formal student prediction.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: A teacher can know the solution while evaluating the student's next step, but giving it to the student changes the task.

    Sources: [OPSD](../../../../post-training/2601.18734-opsd/README-en.md) · [MOPD](../../../../post-training/2606.30406-mopd/README-en.md)

### Can token teacher routing average same-ID logits from different tokenizers? {#cross-mixture-events-before-probabilities}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. Soft routing mixes probabilities over identical events, not generally logits or log-probabilities. Different tokenizers can assign the same ID to different text. CSD aligns textual events and preserves REST mass first. Fine-grained routing cannot fix incompatible event identity.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: Token 17 could be a whole word for one teacher and a fragment for the student; shared numbering does not make them the same event.

    Sources: [Compatibility Matters: A Framework for Token-Level Teacher Selection in On-Policy Distillation](../../../../post-training/2610.21234-token-teacher-selection/README-en.md) · [CSD: Common-Support Distillation for Cross-Tokenizer Knowledge Transfer](../../../../post-training/2610.28895-csd/README-en.md) · [MOPD](../../../../post-training/2606.30406-mopd/README-en.md)

### Does SPOD freeze a successful episode when the teacher disfavors one action? {#cross-success-not-whole-episode-freeze}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. Success and raw complete-action probabilities identify qualifying decisions; only there does SPOD remove distillation and add a soft floor. Other decisions keep learning. MOPD and OPSD do not automatically protect this behavior.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: If step two works despite being unusual, protecting it need not discard useful corrections to steps one and three.

    Sources: [Beyond the Teacher: Understanding and Preserving Distillation Overshoot in Agentic On-Policy Distillation](../../../../post-training/2610.25034-spod/README-en.md) · [MOPD](../../../../post-training/2606.30406-mopd/README-en.md) · [OPSD](../../../../post-training/2601.18734-opsd/README-en.md)

### Does giving an OPSD teacher more visual evidence prove its corrections are visual? {#cross-privilege-not-visual-attribution}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. Language priors, style, and prior prefix mistakes can also change. VAD contrasts evidence presence and removal with the same teacher and student prefix, then projects the original correction. Privileged inputs alone do not supply attribution, and the local proxy is not genuine visual attribution.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: A crop might cause shorter phrasing even if brevity is not supported by the image; compare views to distinguish shared changes.

    Sources: [OPSD](../../../../post-training/2601.18734-opsd/README-en.md) · [VAD](../../../../post-training/2607.28590-vad/README-en.md)

### Does a larger P²-MOPD expert coefficient mean a larger MOPD token-mixture weight for that teacher? {#cross-parameter-prior-not-teacher-mixture}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. A parameter-prior coefficient multiplies a fixed weight-space task vector and changes the student's update direction. Routing or mixture coefficients operate on output supervision distributions. P²-MOPD still needs domain-teacher scoring on student trajectories; a direction coefficient cannot replace that distribution or be read as the same confidence measure.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: Moving a medical task-vector coefficient from 0.25 to 0.3 does not mix every token's medical-teacher probability from 25% to 30%; a neural network's weight-to-output map is nonlinear.

    Sources: [P²-MOPD: Accelerating Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation via Parameter Priors](../../../../post-training/2611.03953-p2-mopd/README-en.md) · [MOPD](../../../../post-training/2606.30406-mopd/README-en.md)

### Can OPSD and Targeted Guidance both be reduced to whole-trajectory teacher KL because both provide extra context? {#cross-feedback-mask-not-global-privilege}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. Targeted Guidance applies full-vocabulary student-to-frozen-teacher KL only at criterion-failing agent turns, keeps all valid response tokens in the denominator and retains ordinary RL rewards. A privileged OPSD reference does not automatically supply these local-failure contracts. Extra information belongs only in the training teacher, not in a deployed student's history as a hint about future errors.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: One failed token with KL 2 among 100 response tokens contributes 2/100. Removing the other 99 tokens before averaging gives 2 and changes the intended strength.

    Sources: [Stabilizing On-Policy Targeted Guidance in Agentic Reinforcement Learning](../../../../post-training/2611.05266-targeted-guidance/README-en.md) · [OPSD](../../../../post-training/2601.18734-opsd/README-en.md)

### When offline F1 is close between two retrieval candidates, can RAGCompass apply the 0.05 threshold at inference? How is this different from OPSD's privileged information? {#cross-ragcompass-offline-gap}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. That threshold filters offline examples with reference answers. Inference uses reranker or comparison-head scores. OPSD feeds the privileged solution to the teacher to change vocabulary predictions; RAGCompass uses reference answers only to define candidate labels, not as scorer inputs.

    **Illustrative example:** Offline F1 values of 0.50 and 0.48 fail the filter. In deployment, scorer values of 0.2 and 0.7 still select the second candidate; true F1 must not be consulted.

    Sources: [RAGCompass: Generalizable Retriever Routing via Reranking](../../../../post-training/2611.05596-ragcompass/README-en.md) · [OPSD](../../../../post-training/2601.18734-opsd/README-en.md)

### Does removing the reference from an OPSD teacher and continuing the student implement BOPD? {#cross-cross-bootstrap-teacher-versus-privileged-view}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. Stage II uses the trained intermediate as teacher but restores the student exactly to the initial model and creates a new optimizer. Removing the reference is only one change; continuing the existing student or reverting the teacher changes the method.

    **Illustrative example:** A weight learned from 1 to 1.2 in Stage I remains 1.2 in the Stage II teacher, while the student returns to 1 with empty optimizer state. Starting both at 1.2 is continuation, not this handoff.

    Sources: [Bootstrapped On-Policy Distillation](../../../../post-training/2611.13680-bopd/README-en.md) · [OPSD](../../../../post-training/2601.18734-opsd/README-en.md)

### Why cannot LCS failure-only updates and SPOD share one success mask? {#cross-cross-whole-success-versus-action-protection}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** LCS skips entire successful episodes. SPOD additionally compares complete-action teacher/student probabilities and protects only qualifying decisions, retaining distillation elsewhere. Mask granularity, reduction and retained losses differ.

    **Illustrative example:** When the teacher supports an action more than the student in a successful episode, SPOD can continue that action's KL. The LCS method still skips the entire successful trajectory.

    Sources: [Which Successes Make Good References? Action-Sequence Alignment for Multi-Turn On-Policy Distillation](../../../../post-training/2611.13135-lcs-reference-opd/README-en.md) · [Beyond the Teacher: Understanding and Preserving Distillation Overshoot in Agentic On-Policy Distillation](../../../../post-training/2610.25034-spod/README-en.md)

## Update log {#updates}

Updates record new approaches, changed trade-offs, and follow-up evidence.

**2026-11-12** · Added same-task LCS selection, separating episode-level failure filtering from SPOD's complete-action protection. Preserved independent free-target assignment, both normalizers and teacher-only references. The CPU selector is not substitute multi-turn agent training.

Affected: [Which Successes Make Good References? Action-Sequence Alignment for Multi-Turn On-Policy Distillation](../../../../post-training/2611.13135-lcs-reference-opd/README-en.md)

**2026-11-12** · Added BOPD to distinguish continued privileged views from two-stage reference-free transfer, preserving student/optimizer restoration and per-trajectory FKL. A100 evidence covers loss/handoff only; full multi-GPU, long-generation experiments are not reproduced.

Affected: [Bootstrapped On-Policy Distillation](../../../../post-training/2611.13680-bopd/README-en.md)

**2026-11-06** · Added RAGCompass evidence-set utility distillation and compared the supervision axis, feedback entry point, and offline-to-deployment boundary with OPSD and Targeted Guidance.

Affected: [RAGCompass: Generalizable Retriever Routing via Reranking](../../../../post-training/2611.05596-ragcompass/README-en.md) · [OPSD](../../../../post-training/2601.18734-opsd/README-en.md) · [Stabilizing On-Policy Targeted Guidance in Agentic Reinforcement Learning](../../../../post-training/2611.05266-targeted-guidance/README-en.md)

**2026-11-05** · Adds P²-MOPD's parameter-prior channels and Targeted Guidance's failed-turn feedback against MOPD teacher supervision and OPSD privileged context, retaining separate update directions, original denominators and cost-deferred full-experiment boundaries.

Affected: [P²-MOPD: Accelerating Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation via Parameter Priors](../../../../post-training/2611.03953-p2-mopd/README-en.md) · [Stabilizing On-Policy Targeted Guidance in Agentic Reinforcement Learning](../../../../post-training/2611.05266-targeted-guidance/README-en.md) · [MOPD](../../../../post-training/2606.30406-mopd/README-en.md) · [OPSD](../../../../post-training/2601.18734-opsd/README-en.md)
